altyazi.metin: A single uranium fuel pellet, the size
of a fingertip, holds about as much
energy as a ton of coal!
Energy Sources, episode four: the atom.
It all starts with fission.
A neutron hits a uranium-235 nucleus,
the nucleus splits in two, releasing
heat and new neutrons.
Those neutrons split other nuclei.
In a reactor, this chain reaction is
kept in constant balance by control
rods.
Uranium is packed into fuel rods as
small ceramic pellets.
Two hundred sixty-four rods form one
fuel assembly, and the assemblies are
placed in the reactor core.
The heat of fission warms water.
In most plants, this hot water turns
water in a second loop into steam.
The steam spins a turbine, and a
generator makes electricity.
The white cloud above cooling towers
isn't smoke; it's water vapor.
The reactor runs inside a thick steel
pressure vessel and a concrete
containment building.
America's largest nuclear power plant is
Plant Vogtle in Georgia.
Its two newest units are AP1000
reactors, and all four units together
make about four thousand six hundred
megawatts.
The enormous energy inside the atom!
Next episode: the heat beneath our feet.
